static_traits.name: Mark
static_traits.social_status: Has a supportive group of friends and running buddies, but has not yet actively shared feelings of inadequacy and inferiority
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no history of psychotherapy or similar psychological problems
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, but often using negative labels (e.g., 'failure'), catastrophic and black-and-white wording, and tending to filter positive information

basic_info.main_problem: Feelings of inadequacy and self-criticism related to marathon results; persistently doubting ability after races, labeling oneself a 'failure', and filtering out past positive running achievements.
basic_info.core_demands: This self-doubt and these feelings of inadequacy are affecting my motivation to participate in future marathon races.
growth_experiences: In a marathon six months ago, setting high expectations of 'top three' but not yet achieving them; persistently ruminating about performance after the race, doubting ability, disparaging oneself with the 'failure' label, and treating past good finishes and training results as 'unimportant'; this experience accompanied by stress and shame, leading to decreased training drive and avoiding running groups.

special_situations.event: Thinking about entering the next marathon
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot place top three or win, it means I am unworthy of recognition and am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to improve performance through self-pressure and positive self-talk, but switching to avoiding training when anxiety rises
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will fail again,I am not good enough

special_situations.event: Recalling the loss at the last marathon
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One failure proves my overall ability is inadequate; past efforts do not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly reflecting and negating positive evidence, reinforcing self-criticism to 'force oneself to improve'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: All my efforts have been wasted

special_situations.event: Meeting running buddies or preparing to join a running group activity
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not perform well, others will look down on me and I will be seen as a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids contact with running partners to reduce the risk of being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am not capable; I am a failure

special_situations.event: Seeing others' race rankings or result shares
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only being better than others counts as valuable; being inferior means failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses goals on rankings and winning or losing, ignoring the process and personal progress
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as others, so I am just a failure

core_conflict.wish: Longs to prove self-worth through excellent performance and rankings, gaining others' recognition and respect
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being seen as incompetent and a 'failure' after failing, encountering shame and negation, losing self-worth
defense_goal: Avoiding further failure and external negation through harsh self-demands and self-criticism
Maintains fragile self-esteem and security by avoiding running groups and others' evaluations

object_relations.self_representation: Inadequate, a competitor/evaluatee who needs to prove oneself through results
object_relations.object_representation: Harsh judges / more accomplished others (running friends/groups)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about running partners or race rankings and performance comparisons
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client tends to believe others will look down on them, seeing themselves as a failure (transference: projecting inner self-denial onto others' gazes)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a gentle clarifying tone; inviting concrete evidence and alternative interpretations; avoiding direct refutation, using open-ended questioning and empathy reflections to help distinguish facts from speculation.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When recalling the last competition loss and feeling intense shame
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Turning outward anger and frustration against the self, reinforcing the 'failure' self-label
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Identifying self-attacking language in an accepting, non-judgmental tone; using gentle reframing and emotion naming; encouraging directing energy toward concrete, feasible training goals and the value of the process.

manifestations: Running once brought freedom and clarity, but one loss led to being completely defined by winning/losing and rankings
Believes the efforts were 'all in vain', downplaying past progress and accomplishments
outcomes: Avoids joining running groups and running activities

manifestations: Having supportive friends yet not sharing true feelings of inadequacy and shame
Avoiding the running group because of self-evaluation
outcomes: Emotional isolation and subjective sense of isolation

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Internalizes the external rule 'must be top three / must win to count as good' as a standard of self-worth
Judges himself by the single indicator of ranking and winning/losing, ignoring process and personal progress

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: When invited to focus on the positive side and process value, quickly returns to the failure narrative
Avoids talking about own true feelings when communicating with running friends

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Assuming others will look down on oneself; seeing oneself as a failure
In social scenes, presumes negative evaluation and thus chooses avoidance

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Constraining oneself with excessively high standards, leading to decreased training drive and avoidance

exception_events.target_problem: When talking about running or thinking about participating in the next marathon, the client typically engages in self-denial, compares with others and feels ashamed, thus reducing training and avoiding running groups.
exception_events.unique_outcome: When exchanging running experiences with friends, briefly not comparing oneself, able to appreciate others' achievements and experience some ease and recognition, with weakened negative self-evaluation.
exception_events.reason: Clue: in a setting where attention was on others' experiences and the perspective shifted toward appreciation and sharing, self-comparison and labeling were temporarily interrupted; the group support atmosphere and focus on the present moment reduced the fixation on rankings.

positive_force: Has supportive friends and a running community
Multiple good training sessions and marathon finishes in the past (having a stable running foundation)
Able to try self-encouragement and positive self-talk
Clearly knowing the sense of freedom and physical/mental pleasure running brings (foundation of intrinsic motivation)
negative_force: Negating the positive / mental filtering; persistently ignoring progress and the value of the process
Strict external performance standards and self-labeling ('failure')
Shame and assumptions of others' negative evaluations lead to avoiding training and socializing

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids running training and running group activities
antecedent: Thinking about participating in the next marathon
Seeing others share results or rankings
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalizing the rigid standard of 'must win / place top three to count as good'; catastrophically anticipating failing again and being negated by others, triggering shame and anxiety.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the negative emotions associated with being evaluated and failing, maintaining self-esteem and a sense of safety in the short term.
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased training drive; reduced physical activity and self-care, further reinforcing self-denial and feelings of failure.

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive self-criticism and labeling (defining oneself as a 'failure')
antecedent: When talking with others about running or seeing others' results
When thinking of setting training goals and ranking requirements
target_behavior.core_reason: Takes external rankings and win-loss standards as the sole basis of self-worth, ignoring process and multidimensional performance, and thus attributes setbacks to the whole self
target_behavior.function: Gains a temporary sense of control and 'spurring' through self-punishment and self-reproach, trying to avoid failing again.
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood and impaired motivation; worsening training and social avoidance; declining life and self-care.
